messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] deploy-canary failed in prod (us-west-2) — spike in 5xx on /v1/inference (canary group). Root TS: 1718501234

deploy-bot: Canary roll 2026.03.15-17:20 started by andrew.t — version inference-service@release-2026-03-15

mike.j: I’m on call, seeing the page. grabbing logs.

mike.j: Paging @maya.k @andrew.t — canary 3/5 failing, 50% errors, latency 2.1s -> 20s backend errors

samir: I see decrypt errors in canary pods: KMS Decrypt failed: PermissionDenied. Looks like KMS key rotated earlier today.

andrew.t: Wait we rolled a config that updated KMS key alias env var in deployment: INFERENCE_KMS_KEY=alias/inference-prod-v2 — I thought staging already had permissions

eva: Canary service account doesn't have iam:Decrypt for new key. The CI rotation job updated alias but cross-account policy not applied.

mike.j: Confirmed: logs:
``` 
2026-03-15T17:21:05Z inference-canary-3 stderr ERROR Failed to decrypt DB creds: AccessDeniedException: User arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/inf-canary-role/... is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:987654:key/abcd-ef12
```

maya.k: Ugh. So the canary is trying to use new key, missing permissions -> 500s. Customer-facing inference endpoints are routed 10% to canary -> causing elevated error rate for all customers. Need kill-switch or rollback.

mike.j: Triage options: 1) toggle feature flag that sends 0% to canary (ff/inference-canary-routing) 2) rollback deployment to release-2026-03-14 3) patch IAM policy to allow Decrypt (requires infra change + IAM review)

mike.j: I'm going to flip the kill-switch flag to stop routing to canary now.

mike.j: Running flag toggle:
```
# internal flags API
curl -s -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://flags.internal.api/ff/inference-canary-routing" \
  -d '{"value":0}'
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag ff/inference-canary-routing set to 0 by mike.j - change propagated to edge within 8s.

incident-bot: Routing change observed — canary traffic drops to 0% (proxy metrics)

andrew.t: Good. Error rate returning to baseline. Starting rollback of canary release to be safe.

andrew.t: Rollback command:
```
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/inference inference=image-release-2026-03-14
kubectl rollout status deploy/inference -w
```

andrew.t: Rollback completed at 17:27 UTC. All pods are back to release-2026-03-14

maya.k: Confirming customer impact: peak error rate 4.7% across US region for ~6 minutes. Approx 3.2k failed requests (estimated). No data exfiltration, only Decrypt failures to KMS.

eva: Notified support: creating incident ticket INC-2026-0315-01, customers with SLA > 99.9: account-ids: 1111,2222,3333 — outreach in progress.

samir: Root cause appears to be a secret alias swap in CI that didn't include updating cross-account IAM bindings for the canary role. The rollout PR included the env var change but infra change was gated.

mike.j: On-call handoff: I'm handing off to maya.k for follow-up, I need to go offline in 20m. Handoff notes: kill-switch toggled, rollback done, customer outreach started, need IAM fix + re-deploy with correct key policy.

maya.k: Taking handoff. Action items: 1) Create infra change to add kms:Decrypt for inf-canary-role on new key 2) Coordinate with security for key policy 3) re-run canary with 1% traffic then monitor 15m

maya.k: I've opened infra ticket INFRA-4567 to add the policy. Attaching minimal IAM snippet:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:987654:key/abcd-ef12",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456:role/inf-canary-role"}
}
```

andrew.t: We should also add a CI check to ensure KMS alias referenced exists in same account or required policy changes are included in the same PR.

mike.j: Postmortem owners: maya.k (ops follow-up), andrew.t (deploy process + CI checks), samir (infra + IAM), eva (customer comms). We'll have a bridge for postmortem at 2026-03-16 1600 UTC.

ops-rotations: oncall handover logged from mike.j -> maya.k at 1718501454

maya.k: Final update: ramped canary to 1% at 18:10 after IAM patch, monitored 25m, no Decrypt errors. Closing incident for now; creating postmortem doc and linking IT.

incident-bot: Incident resolved — severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 for follow-ups. Duration: ~49 minutes. Tags: deploy, kms, feature-flag, rollback

eva: Saved notes in INC-2026-0315-01 and pinged accounts. Will prepare customer summary.

mike.j: Thanks team. Quick follow-ups: add automation to validate KMS aliases and preflight IAM check for canary service accounts. Also add an alert rule to detect sudden KMS Decrypt errors spike.

andrew.t: Agreed. Also will add a canary kill-switch that can be toggled via deploy-bot CLI as backup.
